findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the underlying storage, automated snapshots and logs hold customer data (an EMPLOYEES table with names and addresses) in cleartext. Encryption cannot be enabled in place later without a snapshot/restore cycle.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the database a public DNS name and routable address, moving the MySQL endpoint onto the internet edge where it is exposed to credential stuffing and direct attack. The database is only ever consumed by an EC2 instance inside the same VPC, so no public endpoint is warranted.

The user_data script interpolates var.password and the DB username directly into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext by any process or SSRF-reachable code path on the instance via http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data, and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the master database password.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached through an instance profile to an internet-facing web server, any compromise of the PHP application yields full read/write/delete over every S3 bucket, the ability to launch or modify EC2 resources, and full control of all RDS instances — a direct privilege escalation and data exfiltration path.

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (token-optional). A server-side request forgery or file-inclusion bug in the PHP application on this host can retrieve the instance profile's temporary credentials, which carry the wildcard s3/ec2/rds policy above.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the instance volume — which stores the database password in /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc — is written unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be on.

The parameter group sets only character set options and does not set require_secure_transport = 1. Combined with the PHP client calling mysqli_connect() with no SSL context, application-to-database traffic including the admin credentials travels unencrypted.

The database security group permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised database host has an unconstrained outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control; database instances have no legitimate need for arbitrary internet egress.
The master username is hard-coded to "admin", a well-known default that halves the work of a credential guessing attack against the now internet-reachable endpoint.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the form at /var/www/html/index.php over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration or termination layer, so submitted employee names and addresses cross the network in cleartext.

The master password is supplied through var.password and is therefore persisted in cleartext in Terraform state (and in any plan file), rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or generated with manage_master_user_password. The lifecycle ignore_changes on password does not mitigate state exposure.
